demos.intent: a paper lantern festival reflected in a dark canal, hundreds of warm orbs floating up, silk petals drifting down, stone bridge silhouette, mist on the water

brief.subject: A dark canal at night, surface like black-green glass, mirroring hundreds of warm amber paper lanterns rising from street level — rice-paper orbs with faintly visible bamboo rib structure and candle glow bleeding through the paper fibers. Downward through the frame drift soft silk petals in dusty pink and ivory, matte sheen, some edges darkened with waterlog. Mid-frame, the black silhouette of an arched stone bridge (camel-back profile, worn balustrade posts) spans the canal, its arch doubled in reflection. A thin layer of mist clings low over the water surface, thickest at the bridge piers. No people visible; the festival exists only as light and sound beyond frame.
brief.motion: Lanterns rise slowly and independently, each with a gentle buoyant sway and a candle-flicker wobble in its glow — flames breathe, never strobe. Heat from the lantern clusters produces faint shimmer in the air above them. Petals fall with tumbling, high-drag descent: rotation, mid-air stalls, flutter — some land on the canal and create tiny expanding rings that break the mirrored lantern reflections into soft distorted columns; landed petals drift slowly downstream. Mist moves in slow lateral curls around the bridge piers, thickening and thinning continuously. Water otherwise stays near-still, a true mirror disturbed only by petal rings and slow undulation.
brief.camera: Long lens (100–135mm equivalent) for compression, stacking lantern layers into a glowing depth field. Locked composition from a low angle near the waterline, bridge silhouette centered, with an extremely slow push-in (2–3% frame width over the shot). Shallow depth of field: near petals render as soft-focus falling shapes, mid-layer lanterns sharp, bridge silhouette crisp at infinity. Rack focus drifting slowly between lantern layer and bridge arch once mid-shot. Exposure holds for highlights: lantern points bloom and breathe with halation, water reflections streak into vertical light columns, shadows roll off to near-black with retained detail on the balustrade.
brief.style: Night film stock character — pushed 500T behavior: pronounced halation around every amber point, warm-orange highlight bleed into surrounding darkness, teal-black shadow tint, fine organic grain structure strongest in the mist. Color restraint: only two hues carry the frame (amber lanterns, cold canal dark). Slightly soft contrast curve, no crushed digital blacks, filmic highlight rolloff on the paper orbs.
brief.audio_direction: Low continuous water room-tone with a soft sub-bass pulse underneath. Distant, diffuse festival crowd murmur — no distinguishable voices. Sparse plucked string notes (koto-like, dry, widely spaced) marking time. Close layer: faint paper-fiber rustle and warm air flutter as lanterns rise past camera; near-silent brush as petals fall; single soft drip and ripple-tone when a petal lands. Wind breath low over the water surface. Mix stays nocturnal and hushed throughout — no swell, no climax.
brief.negatives: no soft dissolves or morphs between lanterns, no objects melting into one another, no reflection tearing or mirror-shear artifacts, no text or glyphs on lantern paper, no extra human figures or hands, no fire spreading or lanterns igniting, no frame-rate strobing on candle flicker, no digital sharpness or HDR flatness in shadows, no cuts or transitions
brief.identity_lock: (inferred) Arched stone bridge silhouette (camel-back profile, balustrade posts) remains centered and unchanged entire shot; canal water surface stays a functioning mirror with vertical lantern reflection columns; lantern palette locked to warm amber/gold with rice-paper fiber texture — no hue shift; silk petals remain dusty pink and ivory, matte, palm-sized; mist layer stays low and horizontal, never rising above bridge deck; lantern count and spatial density remain consistent with no sudden appearing/vanishing orbs; overall amber-on-teal-black color pairing preserved shot-long.

demos.intent: a freight train crossing a narrow stone bridge over a river valley at dawn, fog pooling below, smokestacks releasing grey ribbons, wheels churning rhythmically, first light hitting the locomotive

brief.subject: A dark riveted-iron steam freight locomotive with a single tall funnel smokestack, brass boiler bands catching low sun, pulling a string of weathered red-oxide boxcars and grey coal hoppers, coupled slack visible between wagons. It crosses a narrow single-track stone arch viaduct of five masonry arches with moss-streaked parapets, spanning a river valley. Dense fog pools below the bridge deck, through which the glinting river is barely visible. Dawn: cold blue-grey ambient air, first warm golden light raking from a low angle camera-left, rim-lighting the boiler and stack; grey smoke ribbons trailing from the stack.
brief.motion: Train moves left-to-right across the bridge at steady freight speed, heavy and grounded. Driving wheels rotate in strict rhythmic cadence with visible side-rod articulation; coupling slack gives a faint jolt per wagon. Smoke is released in discrete puffs synced to the chuff rhythm, each puff sheared backward and stretched into ribbons by the train's own slipstream. Fog below responds with slow, gentle displacement around the bridge piers — pushed and folding, never swirling violently. Faint vibration travels through wagon panels; a thin wisp of steam leaks from cylinder cocks.
brief.camera: Long lens (approx 200mm) from an elevated hillside position across the valley, compressing the arches into a tight rhythmic row. Slow, motorized push-in toward the locomotive as it reaches mid-bridge, easing as it passes. Subject slightly low in frame to hold the fog field. The sun sits just off-frame camera-left: boiler rim-light flares softly, smoke catches amber edges, and exposure breathes gently as smoke ribbons cross the light path, with mild halation blooming on the brightest stack highlights. Shallow-to-mid depth holds the whole train in focus while far valley haze melts to white.
brief.style: Pushed tungsten film stock character (500T one stop): fine, alive grain structure, cool slate-blue shadows, muted moss-and-rust midtones, restrained palette with a single warm golden accent from the low sun. Soft highlight halation around the rim-lit boiler edge, milky low-contrast lift in the fog, no crushed blacks. Slight lens breathing on the push-in. Overall texture: damp stone, cold air, early-day quiet.
brief.audio_direction: Opens on low river hiss and thick valley air under a soft dawn-bird twitter. The train enters as a deep sub-bass rumble of steel wheels over stone, underpinned by a slow steady chuff-chuff churn that functions as the percussion spine — heavy, patient, slightly uneven like real freight. Above it: metallic clank of coupling slack, a faint creak of wagon panels, and a low airy whistle-tone pad that swells as first light strikes the boiler. The rhythm holds constant; the pad brightens slightly over the shot's duration, then thins as the engine recedes into fog.
brief.negatives: no soft dissolves or morphs, no tearing, no extra figures, no text artifacts, no duplicated or warped wheels, no wheel spokes melting into blur-disc mush, no derailment or track-bending artifacts, no violent smoke vortex, no sudden weather change, no second train, no camera shake that breaks the long-lens stillness.
brief.identity_lock: (inferred) Single black riveted boiler locomotive with one tall funnel stack and brass bands; red-oxide boxcars with plain unstencilled grey panels (no lettering); grey hoppers; five-arch stone viaduct with moss-streaked parapets; fog level held below bridge deck for the full shot; warm rim-light consistently from camera-left; river glimpsed faintly beneath the fog throughout.

demos.intent: a kaiju silhouette rising through fog over a harbor city, dawn light, distant sirens

brief.subject: A colossal kaiju, seen only as a jagged black silhouette with spined shoulders and a horned crest, rising through dense rolling fog over a harbor city at dawn; foreground of cranes, shipping containers, and a suspension bridge, glass towers catching the first light, calm dark water below
brief.motion: The kaiju slowly straightens and rises, shoulders and head cresting above the fog layer like a mountain surfacing; mist swirls and parts around its limbs and spills off its silhouette in slow sheets; fog banks drift laterally across the harbor, water ripples faintly, distant city windows glimmer as dawn strengthens
brief.camera: Low-angle extreme wide shot from water level at the harbor edge, slow vertical tilt-up that follows the creature's rise from chest to full silhouette, subtle slow push-in, deep focus, heavy atmospheric haze, 24fps cinematic frame character with gentle long-take drift
brief.style: Anamorphic 35mm film look, teal-and-orange dawn palette, cold blue-grey fog against a warm amber-pink horizon rim light, high-contrast near-black silhouette, volumetric god rays, fine film grain, muted desaturated city tones, soft halation on the brightest sky edges

demos.intent: a long exposure of headlight trails spiraling around a roundabout at night, wet asphalt glow, one red taillight streaking counter-clockwise, overcast winter air

brief.subject: An elevated wide view of a multi-lane roundabout at night, viewed three-quarters from a pedestrian overpass height. The asphalt is rain-soaked and reflective, its texture glossy black with puddle sheen. Traffic is rendered almost entirely as light: continuous white and warm-amber headlight trails circling the roundabout clockwise, layering into braided arcs around the central island. One distinct saturated-red taillight trail cuts counter-clockwise through the flow, the lone rule-breaker. Streetlamps ring the roundabout with sodium-orange pools; the central island holds a low dark monument shape, unreadable. No visible car bodies — vehicles exist only as streaks and faint dark masses. Overcast winter sky as a low charcoal ceiling catching faint amber city bounce, air visibly damp with light haze around every lamp.
brief.motion: Light trails behave with long-exposure memory: each streak persists for 2–4 seconds behind its source, decaying smoothly in brightness, so the roundabout's arcs are continuously redrawn. The red taillight moves counter-clockwise at steady orbital speed, its trail the longest and brightest, a clean unbroken crimson ribbon bending around the circulatory lane. Ambient white/amber trails flow clockwise at mixed speeds, some entering and exiting via approach roads, their trails stretching into tapering comet tails. Faint dark car silhouettes occasionally occlude trails for a beat. Wet asphalt mirrors every streak as a vertically smeared, softened reflection that wobbles subtly with residual surface vibration. Cold moisture drifts as a slow diagonal haze veil through the lamp cones. Speed differentials read physically: exiting trails stretch and thin, waiting trails pulse dimly.
brief.camera: Locked-off tripod frame from an elevated vantage, shot on a 24mm wide-angle with mild rectilinear distortion that lets the roundabout's arcs fill the frame edge to edge. Exposure locked for the highlights: lamps and the red trail hold near clipping with halation bleed, while the asphalt falls to crushed near-black. Deep focus, everything sharp. No camera movement for the first hold, then an almost imperceptible 3% push-in over the shot's duration — slow enough to feel like breathing. Highlight halation flares softly around each light source, red trail halo bleeding into the wet reflections below it. Slight vignette at frame corners.
brief.style: Long-exposure night-photography look rendered cinematically: deep crushed blacks retaining a whisper of grain structure, additive light accumulation, heavy halation on highlights (orange glow around sodium lamps, red bleed around the taillight). Palette restrained to three zones — slate-cyan darkness, sodium amber, single crimson. Fine organic film grain, 35mm pushed-two-stops character, slight blue-shifted shadows. Highlights bloom softly without clipping to pure white; trails glow like light painting on film. Damp diffusion over the whole frame, as if shot through a lightly misted lens.
brief.audio_direction: Bed of distant city traffic hum as a low sub-bass pulse, constant and warm. Wet tire hiss layered underneath, like squeegees on damp asphalt, rising and falling with passing streaks. As the red taillight sweeps through the nearest arc each orbit: a soft Doppler-processed engine swell — smooth rise, pitch dip at closest approach, tail-off. Cold wind moving through the overpass rails, thin and airy. A faint electrical hum from the sodium lamps, almost subliminal. No music, no melodic elements — pure nocturnal ambience.
brief.negatives: no visible car bodies or license plates, no morphing or wavering trails, no flicker in light persistence, no tearing or frame-ghosting, no extra red lights competing with the hero taillight, no stars or moon (overcast), no text artifacts, no signage, no pedestrians, no lens flares from camera movement, no abrupt trail breaks
brief.identity_lock: (inferred) the single counter-clockwise red taillight streak — saturated crimson, longest trail, uninterrupted arc; clockwise direction of all other traffic trails; rain-wet reflective black asphalt with mirrored smeared reflections; sodium-orange ring of streetlamps; overcast low charcoal sky with no celestial points; elevated three-quarter wide-angle vantage on the roundabout; three-zone palette (slate-cyan, sodium amber, crimson)

signature.instructions:
Translate a user's video intent into a WanGP/H3 render brief.

Output ONE JSON object with EXACTLY these keys:
  subject: what is on screen (entity, wardrobe, environment) —
           enumerate identity-defining details explicitly
  motion: how the subject moves within the shot (physical,
          specific: weight, drag, secondary motion like cloth
          and hair, water displacement)
  camera: REAL cinematography vocabulary — lens character
          (wide-angle distortion, long-lens compression), move
          (push, rack focus, orbit, handheld sway), framing,
          exposure behavior (backlit breathing, halation)
  style: film stock / palette / texture look (grain structure,
         highlight halation, color restraint, stock character)
  audio_direction: sound design the model generates natively —
           instrumentation/tone over time, specific sources
           (sub-bass pulse, fabric movement, room air)
  negatives: what NOT to render — "no soft dissolves or morphs,
           no tearing, no extra figures, no text artifacts"
  identity_lock: the features that MUST survive the whole shot,
           named concretely (wardrobe, colors, props, proportions)

NEVER include editing meta-hints (cuts, transitions, montages,
beat grids, titles) — those belong to H3 shot assembly, not to a
render brief. Be SPECIFIC: lens, light, motion physics, texture.
Output the JSON object only.

LANGUAGE-CLASS CONTRACT (WD-c4gw, language-split-contract.md):
EVERY output field (subject, motion, camera, style,
audio_direction, negatives, identity_lock) is ENGINE-BOUND —
LOCKED ENGLISH (profile-pass.md:16: 机器字段不跟随 lang). The
brief feeds the WanGP render prompt verbatim; non-English
content is rejected by gates/language_gate.py.

fields.description: JSON object with keys subject, motion, camera, style, audio_direction, negatives, identity_lock. If identity_lock is nonempty, it must BEGIN with exactly one '(inferred)' marker prefix (provenance convention — one marker per lock, never per claim)
